figures.depicts: Two coronal brain sections compared. In the younger adult the brain fills the cranial vault; in the older adult it is shrunken, with a wide dark subdural space and a large subdural hemorrhage, and an inset magnifies a torn/stretched bridging vein running to the dura mater. Labelled: subdural space, meninges (dura mater), torn/stretched bridging vein, subdural hemorrhage, skull, brain.

cards.why: depicts exactly the card's mechanism — shrinkage, the opened subdural space, and the torn bridging vein

figures.depicts: Two labelled line drawings of a newborn skull. A top-down view labels the anterior fontanelle where the sutures cross and the posterior fontanelle at the back; a lateral view labels the anterior, mastoid and sphenoidal fontanelles. The soft gaps are tinted blue between the cranial bones.

cards.why: the plate IS the structure the card defines; labels sit on the back so they cue nothing
Parker asked for this plate on the fontanelle cards; it shows the two the card times, and the answers are months so nothing leaks
Parker asked for this plate on the fontanelle cards; it shows where to palpate, and the answers are depressed/bulging so nothing leaks
